key_insight: A Cosserat rod can be reformulated as a chain of rigid nodes with pairwise compliant forces/moments, while retaining the rigor and anti-locking benefits of a mixed finite element derivation.
engineering_relevance: This gives a robust, two-node-coupled rod model suitable for soft robotics and slender-structure dynamics, with simpler discrete mechanics than dense reduced-order strain models.
method: Mixed Petrov–Galerkin Cosserat rod FEM with linear kinematic interpolation
Internal virtual work integrated by midpoint rule; external and inertial terms by trapezoidal rule
Independent stress DOFs in compliance form for dilatation, shear, torsion, and curvature
evidence_signal: Three numerical examples—varying cross sections, tendon-driven actuation, and coupled longitudinal-torsional dynamics—show accuracy, robustness, and convergence.
watch_item: The formulation’s accuracy depends on correct discrete integration and pairwise coupling setup, so implementation details may be critical for stability and consistency.
paper_title: A Mixed Discrete Cosserat Rod Formulation
